![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/bfdf3147fb8488c3a0032f9dad326b5d8c3ff68be46738dc39215e5098af6272.png)
Consider the standard matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^2 \to \mathbb{R}^3$ shown above. What is the value of $a-b?$
e-5518.worked_solution:
Given the vector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/35814ac6d965ac688907d162b45d9b0b194ea40375d4e474466e4fb4b1de1c1b.png) we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-8 & -5 \\ -3 & -6 \\ -4 & 5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-8x-5y \\ -3x-6y \\ -4x+5y\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-5y-8x \\ -3x-6y \\ 5y-4x\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ is given by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/f59824c26875665fcbd8adfc5414fa7b0c60254e01f725f9ca72cf1d370a3e8b.png)

Finally, $a-b=(-5)-(-4)=-1.$

e-5519.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map
e-5519.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $\mathbf{v}$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}:\mathbb{R}^3 \to \mathbb{R}^2,$ find $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v}).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14057898/assets/7a6d4db6774da29f9b89996e348fad61b281737db6b44e9a39efa016fa2f15f3.png)
e-5519.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{v})=T\cdot \mathbf{v},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3 \\ 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 7\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 1
?

Find the standard matrix that represents the linear transformation T:R3→R2, where T:[xyz]⟶[2x−y+zx−y−z].

a
[2−111−11000]
b
[21111001]
c
[00002−511]
d
[2100−5100]
e
[2−111−1−1]
Submit

decision.explanation: The standard matrix has rows given by the coefficients of x, y, and z in each output coordinate: (2,-1,1) and (1,-1,-1). Thus option e produces exactly (2x-y+z, x-y-z).

after.name: Question 1
after.problem:

$$

$$
after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x+(-1)y+1z \\ 1x+(-1)y+(-1)z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x-y+z \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}2x-y+z \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x+(-1)y+1z \\ 1x+(-1)y+(-1)z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}2x-y+z \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}2 & -1 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Question 2
?

Find the standard matrix that represents the linear transformation T:R3→R2, where T:[xyz]⟶[0x−y−z].

a
[000000000]
b
[0000001−1−1]
c
None of the listed
d
[111−1−101−1−4]
e
[000−1−1−1000]
Submit

decision.explanation: The standard matrix is a 2×3 matrix with rows (0,0,0) and (1,-1,-1), producing (0,x-y-z). Every listed matrix is 3×3, so none represents this transformation.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}0 \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0x+0y+0z \\ 1x+(-1)y+(-1)z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the standard matrix that represents the linear transformation T:R3→R2, where T:[xyz]⟶[0x−y−z].

EXPLANATION

We require a 2×3 matrix T such that T⋅[xyz]=[0x+0y+0z1x+(−1)y+(−1)z].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}0 \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0x+0y+0z \\ 1x+(-1)y+(-1)z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ x-y-z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 1 & -1 & -1\end{aligned}].
$$

Find the standard matrix that represents the linear transformation T:R3→R4, where T:[xyz]⟶[7x−3yx−2y+z0z].

b
[7−301−21000001]

Submit

decision.explanation: The four output coordinates give coefficient rows (7,-3,0), (1,-2,1), (0,0,0), and (0,0,1). These form the 4×3 matrix in option b.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{4},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7x-3y \\ x-2y+z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}].$
after.worked_solution:
We require a $4\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7x+(-3)y+0z \\ 1x+(-2)y+1z \\ 0x+0y+0z \\ 0x+0y+1z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7x-3y \\ x-2y+z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{4},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}7x-3y \\ x-2y+z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
We require a $4\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7x+(-3)y+0z \\ 1x+(-2)y+1z \\ 0x+0y+0z \\ 0x+0y+1z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}7x-3y \\ x-2y+z \\ 0 \\ z\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}7 & -3 & 0 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}(-3)x+(-5)y+2z \\ 2x+(-3)y+0z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3x-5y+2z \\ 2x-3y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

EXPLANATION

We require a 2×3 matrix T such that T⋅[xyz]=[(−3)x+(−5)y+2z2x+(−3)y+0z].

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where
$T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-3x-5y+2z \\ 2x-3y\end{aligned}].$
content.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that
    

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}(-3)x+(-5)y+2z \\ 2x+(-3)y+0z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that
    

$$
[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-3x-5y+2z \\ 2x-3y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is
    

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -5 & 2 \\ 2 & -3 & 0\end{aligned}].
$$

decision.explanation: In x,y,z order, the output coefficients are (1,-3,8) and (1,2,1), since x+z+2y=x+2y+z. These are the rows of option e.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x-3y+8z \\ x+z+2y\end{aligned}].
$$
after.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1x+(-3)y+8z \\ 1x+2y+1z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x-3y+8z \\ x+z+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Standard Matrix of a Linear Transformation
content.problem:
Find the standard matrix that  represents  the  linear  transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ where

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}x-3y+8z \\ x+z+2y\end{aligned}].
$$
content.worked_solution:
We require a $2\times 3$ matrix $T$ such that

$$
T\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}1x+(-3)y+8z \\ 1x+2y+1z\end{aligned}].
$$

Notice that

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}x-3y+8z \\ x+z+2y\end{aligned}].
$$

Therefore, the matrix which represents the linear transformation $T$ is

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 8 \\ 1 & 2 & 1\end{aligned}].
$$

after.name: Question 6
after.problem:
$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}],\,T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}ay+3z-x \\ bz-2x+cy\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the standard matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2}$ shown above. What is the value of $a+b+c?$
after.worked_solution:
Given the vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]\,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-1 & 0 & 3 \\ -2 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-x+0y+3z \\ -2x+4y+2z\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0y+3z-x \\ 2z-2x+4y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $T$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y \\ z\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}0y+3z-x \\ 2z-2x+4y\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+b+c=0+2+4=6.$

after.name: Question 9
after.problem:
$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -2 & -8 \\ -9 & 7\end{aligned}],\,T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-3x+y \\ ax-8y \\ -9x+by\end{aligned}]
$$

Consider the standard matrix $T$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3}$ shown above. What is the value of $a+b?$
after.worked_solution:
Given the vector $\,[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]\,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}-3 & 1 \\ -2 & -8 \\ -9 & 7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}-3x+y \\ -2x-8y \\ -9x+7y\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the linear transformation $T$ is given by

$$
T:[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]⟶[\begin{aligned}-3x+y \\ -2x-8y \\ -9x+7y\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a+b=-2+7=5.$

after.name: Question 11
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3},$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7 \\ -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{3},$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 2 \\ 2 & 1 \\ 3 & -5\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 7 \\ -9\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

verification.explanation: Rechecking gives -4(-3)+5(4)-6=26 and 5(-3)-2(4)-7(-6)=19, matching the revealed solution and option a. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option e.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Vector Under a Linear Map
content.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -7\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ -6\end{aligned}]
$$
content.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 5 & 1 \\ 5 & -2 & -7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}-3 \\ 4 \\ -6\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}26 \\ 19\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{2},$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 & -1 & 2 \\ 1 & 4 & -2\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}2 \\ 1 \\ -1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 8\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem:
Consider the matrix $T$ and the vector $v$ given below. If $T$ is the standard matrix of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{4},$ find $T(v).$

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 \\ 6 & -7\end{aligned}],\,v=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}]
$$
after.worked_solution:
Using the fact that $\,T(v)=T\cdot v,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}T(v) & =T\cdot v \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4 & 0 \\ 3 & -2 \\ 5 & 1 \\ 6 & -7\end{aligned}]\cdot [\begin{aligned}3 \\ -2\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-12 \\ 13 \\ 13 \\ 32\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$
